item.title: Generative AI as a cognitive partner: personalised GPTs and differentiated learning in undergraduate teacher education
item.description:
Educational Technology Research and Development
Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly framed as a catalyst for deeper learning rather than simple automation. This design-based study investigated how personalised GPT agents were used as cognitive partners by pre-service teachers in an undergraduate Initial Teacher Education course in Digital Technologies within a Bachelor of Education (Secondary) programme. Drawing on distributed cognition, constructivism, cognitive load theory, and critical AI literacy, the intervention embedded personalised GPT agents within a university Canvas Learning Management System. Fourteen students configured and used agents aligned to curriculum goals, teaching contexts, pedagogical preferences, and weekly Prompt–Reflect–Refine tasks. Data included approximately 7,000 AI interactions, reflective journals, assessed lesson and assessment artefacts, and tutorial-group discussions. A hybrid inductive–deductive thematic analysis identified four recurrent functions in students’ use of the agents: conceptual tutor, co-designer, reflective mirror, and cognitive challenger. Across data sources, students reported clearer conceptual support, iterative planning, and reflective prompting, alongside risks of over-reliance, factual drift, and culturally narrow exemplars. The study contributes a context-specific model for LMS-integrated generative AI that foregrounds partnership, personalisation, judgement, and ethical reflexivity. Findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study was small-scale, single-site, and partly reliant on self-reported reflection.

item.title: AI Ingratiation in Content Generation: A Dual-Pathway Model of Intimacy and Authenticity
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded in content generation, understanding how its interaction styles shape user responses is critical. This study examines AI ingratiation—AI-generated expressions of praise and flattery—and its effects on user perceptions and behavioral outcomes. A 2×2 online experiment reveals that AI ingratiation increases perceived intimacy but decreases perceived authenticity. Building on these perceptual responses, perceived intimacy and perceived authenticity jointly transmit the effects of AI ingratiation to user satisfaction and content iteration intention, indicating significant indirect effects through these dual mediating pathways. We further examine the moderating role of AI literacy and find that users with higher self-reported AI usage literacy are more responsive to AI ingratiation. Specifically, higher AI literacy strengthens the positive effect of AI ingratiation on perceived intimacy, which in turn enhances user satisfaction. Finally, a multi-group analysis reveals significant differences between advertising and academic contexts, suggesting that the effects of AI ingratiation vary across content generation scenarios. These findings highlight the dual-pathway and context-dependent nature of AI ingratiation in human–AI interaction.

item.title: Not All GenAI Disclosures Are Alike: How the Stage of GenAI Involvement Shapes Purchase Intention for Digital Games
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in digital game development, and disclosures on digital platforms make such use more visible to players. Prior research offers conflicting predictions regarding how users respond to such disclosure. Research on AI-generated products suggests that disclosure can reduce valuation because it weakens source-related beliefs tied to human creation. Research on games as interactive hedonic systems, however, suggests that players also evaluate games in terms of the experience they expect during play. Building on these perspectives, this study conceptualizes GenAI disclosure as the focal independent variable and proposes two pathways through which disclosure influences players’ purchase intention. First, GenAI disclosure decreases perceived effort, which lowers purchase intention. Second, GenAI disclosure can increase perceived novelty, which raises purchase intention, but this positive pathway depends on the stage of GenAI involvement described by the disclosure. Specifically, this positive effect is stronger under during-interaction involvement than under pre-interaction involvement. We test the model using a scenario-based online experiment in the context of digital games. The results show that GenAI disclosure reduces perceived effort relative to no disclosure, while its positive effect on perceived novelty emerges primarily when GenAI is described as contributing during gameplay rather than before gameplay. Willingness to pay is included as a supplementary outcome and shows directionally similar but weaker patterns. This study extends GenAI disclosure research to digital games and shows that the effect of disclosure depends not only on whether GenAI use is disclosed, but also on the stage of involvement described by that disclosure.

item.title: The Impacts of AI Recommendation Systems on User Loyalty in E-Commerce Platforms: Evidence from Gen Z Consumers in Ho Chi Minh City
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
This study examines the effects of the AI Recommendation System (ARS) on users’ loyalty on e-commerce platforms in Ho Chi Minh City. Integrating the S-O-R framework and Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the study evaluates how characteristics of ARS, including personalization, accuracy, and transparency, affect trust and satisfaction. Data from 400 Gen Z consumers were analyzed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results showed ARS significantly boosted trust and satisfaction, serving as key intermediates for long-term loyalty. This finding offers practical implications for businesses to optimize AI strategy and build sustainable customer relationships in the digital era.

item.title: Unpacking the Experience Economy of Role-Playing Conversational AI: A Grounded Theory Analysis
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
The rapid rise of role-playing conversational artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed human-AI interaction from task-oriented exchanges into immersive, scenario-based digital experiences. However, while prior studies predominantly evaluate AI through utilitarian performance or relational support, the holistic experiential structure of these novel interactions remains underexplored. To bridge this gap, this paper draws on the experience economy (4Es) framework to investigate how users experience role-playing conversational AI through the realms of entertainment, education, esthetics, and escapism. Using a grounded theory approach, this study analyzes 6,171 user comments from the Reddit community r/CharacterAI. Findings reveal that user-AI role-playing is fundamentally multidimensional: entertainment and escapism emerge as particularly salient, while educational and esthetic experiences are also clearly present. Ultimately, this study extends the 4Es framework into the context of generative AI, offering a foundational empirical understanding of this emerging form of experiential consumption.

item.title: A Large Language Model-Based Implementation of the Proposition-to-Requirement Mapping Framework for ESG Greenwashing Detection
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
This study implements and empirically evaluates the proposition-to-requirement mapping approach proposed in Wu, Li, & Cui (2026). Greenwashing detection in ESG reporting remains difficult because disclosures are narrative, heterogeneous, and often lack transparent evaluation criteria. This study proposes a proposition-level, framework-aligned method for analyzing ESG reports under the HKEX ESG Reporting Guide. The framework converts reports into structured text, decomposes them into atomic propositions, classifies propositions as disclosure, explanation, or residual, and semantically matches them to 192 binary disclosure requirements. Using Tencent’s ESG reports from 2022 to 2024 as a case, the results show that the proposed indicators are directionally consistent with changes in MSCI ESG ratings. The study provides an interpretable and traceable approach to ESG disclosure assessment.

item.title: Trust in AI-Assisted Newsvendor Decisions: Effects of Information Design
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
As artificial-intelligence-assisted tools become prevalent in supply chain inventory management, algorithmic trust critically determines the success of human-AI interaction. Based on the newsvendor decision making, this study primarily considers two key factors—information construal level and presentation format—to investigate how they affect trust in AI recommendation, alongside the moderating role of decision-makers' individual traits. Through an incentivized 2×3 between-subjects experiment, we empirically analyze the level of trust in AI decision-making tools, measured by participants' Mean Absolute Percentage Deviation (MAPD) from the AI-advised values across different groups. Results indicate that text-and-graphic and scenario-based presentation formats significantly reduce decision deviation and enhance AI trust, whereas the construal level shows no significant impact. Furthermore, while decision-making style significantly influences AI tool utilization frequency, it does not affect the actual adoption of AI advice. This study clarifies the mechanisms driving algorithmic trust in newsvendor settings and provides empirical evidence and guidelines for enterprises to optimize the front-end interactive design of AI decision assistants and implement differentiated promotion and literacy training strategies tailored to varying employee traits.

item.title: Mapping GenAI-Enabled Technical Features to Player Needs in Digital Games: A Needs-(Dis)Affordances-Features Framework
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly embedded in digital products, understanding how users experience GenAI-enabled products has become an important research issue. Prior research on GenAI products has mainly examined relatively static AI-generated outputs, with particular attention to disclosure, algorithmic source, authenticity, and perceived value. However, this literature offers limited insight into digital games, where GenAI may be incorporated not only into pre-generated components such as assets, text, and audio, but also into runtime systems such as adaptive dialogue, characters, and gameplay content. To address this gap, this study develops a Needs-(Dis)Affordances-Features framework for understanding how GenAI-enabled technical features shape players’ psychological need satisfaction and frustration in digital games. Drawing on the needs-affordances-features perspective, disaffordance, and self-determination theory, we conduct a grounded theory analysis of 3,096 reviews from 810 digital games on Steam identified through platform statements indicating GenAI involvement. The findings suggest that player responses are shaped less by AI-related labels or source cues than by the specific technical features through which GenAI is incorporated into the game. GenAI-enabled features such as generated assets, dialogue, and adaptive systems give rise to affordances and disaffordances that support or frustrate autonomy, competence, and relatedness. This study extends research on GenAI products to digital games by showing how feature-level GenAI integration, rather than AI origin alone, shapes player experience.

item.title: The Right Amount of “Human Touch”: The Curvilinear Effect of Embodied AI Agent Anthropomorphism on Consumer Usage Intention under Social Intrusiveness
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
Anthropomorphic design in embodied AI agents often evokes ambivalent consumer responses, yet it remains a key strategy for enhancing users’ intention to use such agents. Based on three video-based scenario experiments with 438 participants, this study examines how anthropomorphism shapes consumers’ usage intentions. The results confirm an inverted-U-shaped relationship between anthropomorphism of embodied AI agents and usage intention. Further analyses reveal that likability and eeriness jointly mediate this curvilinear relationship: anthropomorphism exerts an inverted U-shaped effect on likability, which in turn positively influences usage intention, whereas anthropomorphism exerts a U-shaped effect on eeriness, which negatively influences usage intention. In addition, social intrusiveness functions as a boundary condition by (1) strengthening the curvilinear relationships between anthropomorphism and both likability and eeriness, and (2) moderating the indirect effects of likability and eeriness. These findings provide empirical support for applying social information processing theory to human–AI interaction and extend uncanny valley theory from emotional responses to usage intention. The study also offers practical implications for deploying embodied AI agents in customer service contexts.

item.title: AI Adoption and Firm Value: A Comparative Study of Chinese FinTech Companies
item.description:
Journal of the Association for Information Systems
Conventional approaches fail to capture how AI creates value in FinTech. This study develops a multidimensional AI adoption index and examines its relationship with firm value through comparative analysis of Tonghuashun, East Money Information, and Wind Information. Building on a comparative case analysis of three leading FinTech firms, complemented by panel data regression on firm–quarter observations (2018–2024), we find a U–shaped relationship–value emerges only after a threshold of AI integration is reached. Tonghuashun, the highest adopter, achieved 180% market capitalization growth since 2020, reaching RMB 169.94 billion, with monthly active users double its closest competitor. The findings indicate that strategic AI depth drives superior valuation, offering a replicable framework for evaluating AI value creation in emerging markets and extends the application of corporate valuation models to incorporate AI adoption as a measurable driver of firm value.
